title: Two-loop integrals for ttbar gamma production at hadron colliders in the leading-colour approximation
description: 2-loop planar 5-point pentagon-box, 2 on-shell tops + photon + 2 massless; 3 massive internal lines; 142 MIs, 3 elliptic sectors + 2 nested-root doublets [Euclidean fallback point]
mapping_notes: All p outgoing, sum p=0, d_ij=p_i.p_j. Independent p1..p4 (p5 eliminated; propagators only use p1..p4). d13=d45-d12-d23-mt2, d14=d23-d15-d45, d24=d15-d23-d34; p1^2=p2^2=mt2, p3^2=p4^2=0. Order D1..D11 kept, k1,k2 as in paper. Planar ordering (1,5,4,2,3) for PB_E and (3,1,5,4,2) for PB_F: adjacent channels s13,s15,s45,s24,s23; Euclidean fallback makes them all negative (all F coefficients positive). PHYSICAL point X1 of ancillary Boundary_values/PBF_X1.m (s45 channel, above thresholds); no causal object written: relies on DiffExp's derived Feynman (F-i0) contour, which may be refused for 2-loop levels (docs: statements 1-2 only). Euclidean fallback ttgamma_PBF_euclid.json at d12=-1,d23=-1,d34=1,d45=-2,d15=-1,mt2=1.

point.note: Euclidean fallback point (all F coefficients positive). The paper only quotes values at paper_point, a physical point where DiffExp 2.2 cannot yet derive every causal side, so reference_values are not compared here.

normalization: Paper eq.(9): e^{eps gamma_E} d^dk/(i pi^{d/2}) per loop, D=k^2-m^2 (Minkowski, +i0). j_paper[nu] = (-1)^{sum nu} e^{2 eps gamma_E} j_DiffExp[nu]; for both requested index vectors sum nu = 7 -> j_paper = -e^{2eps gamma_E} j_DE. Masters mi[...] contain eps^4 (two-loop starts eps^-4), values given through eps^4 i.e. j through eps^0. DiffExp FT: denominators D=m^2-q^2 (Euclidean-positive), measure prod d^dk/(i pi^{d/2}), no exp(L eps gamma_E) (see de22/docs/amflow-comparison.md, feynman-families.md). Paper Minkowski integral with (q^2-m^2+i0) denominators = (-1)^{sum nu} * DiffExp value (numerator powers included in sum nu).
confidence: high for family (verbatim Table 1) and reference (ancillary basis+values parsed directly); physical-point contour derivation is the risk.
